title: A small dense set of representable hypercovers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

There is a small set $\mathcal H_0$ of hypercovers with varying targets which is dense. More precisely there is an uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa$, in the working universe and larger than the cardinality of the arrows of $\mathcal C$, such that every hypercover admits a refinement whose total number of representable summands in all degrees is less than $\kappa$. A set of representatives up to isomorphism of the hypercovers satisfying this bound can be chosen as $\mathcal H_0$.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Definition 6.1 and Proposition 6.6 with its proof, pp. 16, 18-19 (published numbering: Proposition 6.7); Choudhury--Gallauer, Fact 5.2.

proof.text: Choose an infinite cardinal $\mu\geq\max(\aleph_0,|\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal C|)$ in the working Grothendieck universe and put $\kappa=\mu^+$. This is still in that universe and is uncountable and regular: if fewer than $\kappa$ ordinals below $\kappa$ were cofinal, there would be at most $\mu$ of them, each of cardinality at most $\mu$, so their union would have cardinality at most $\mu$, contradicting cofinality in $\mu^+$. Throughout we construct degrees with at most $\mu$ summands; finite products and countable unions of sets of size at most $\mu$ have size at most $\mu$. The case of an empty category has no targets and the empty collection already works.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Proposition 6.6 proof (p. 19); explicit cardinal and recursion details supplied here.

proof.text: Work with formal families of objects as in [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], realized by $\{A_i\}_{i\in I}\mapsto\coprod_i h_{A_i}$. This realization identifies morphisms of families with presheaf morphisms between these coproducts: a map out of $h_A$ is determined by the image of $\operatorname{id}_A$, which is a unique pair $(i,A\to A_i)$; naturality then gives its value on every arrow $B\to A$. Thus the given hypercover, including its augmentation and all operators, can be regarded as a simplicial formal family. In the construction below a split truncated family means that in each degree $q$ its indices are uniquely pairs $(\sigma,i)$ with $\sigma:[q]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ and $i$ a chosen nondegenerate index in degree $r$; the corresponding component is the same object as at $i$. All matching objects are nevertheless computed in presheaves, never in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Proposition 6.6 proof (p. 19); explicit cardinal and recursion details supplied here.

proof.text: For the given $U_\bullet\to h_T$, apply [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts] to $U_0\to h_T$ and the section $\operatorname{id}_T$. Obtain a covering sieve $R$ of $T$ and, for each $u:A\to T$ in $R$, choose $x_u\in U_0(A)$ mapping to $u$. Let $V_0=\coprod_{u\in R}h_A$, with the maps to $U_0$ determined by $x_u$. Its augmentation is locally surjective: for $b:B\to T$, the sieve $b^*R$ covers by pullback stability and supplies local lifts. By the reverse implication of the same cited criterion, $V_0^\#\to h_T^\#$ is epi. There are at most $\mu$ summands, and the degree-zero family is split, taking every index to be nondegenerate.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Proposition 6.6 proof (p. 19); explicit cardinal and recursion details supplied here.

proof.text: Inductively assume a split $n$-truncated $V$ over $h_T$, a compatible refinement $f_{\leq n}:V_{\leq n}\to U_{\leq n}$, all matching maps covering through degree $n$, and at most $\mu$ summands in each degree. For $A\in\mathcal C$, each $V_q(A)=\coprod_i\operatorname{Hom}(A,V_{q,i})$ has cardinality at most $\mu$. Put $M=M_{n+1}V$, the presheaf of compatible proper faces over $h_T$. Its sections embed into the finite product of the lower-degree section sets (and $h_T(A)$); compatibility only cuts out a subset. Hence $|M(A)|\leq\mu$, including the degree-one matching object $V_0\times_{h_T}V_0$. There are at most $\mu$ pairs $(A,b)$ with $b\in M(A)$, since objects inject into arrows via their identities. The truncated refinement gives a map $M\to M_{n+1}U$ by applying $f$ to every face.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Proposition 6.6 proof (p. 19); explicit cardinal and recursion details supplied here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts] to the given matching map $U_{n+1}\to M_{n+1}U$. For every pair $(A,b)$ from the preceding step, choose a covering sieve $R_{A,b}$ on $A$ and, for each $u:B\to A$ in it, a section $x_{A,b,u}\in U_{n+1}(B)$ whose boundary is the image of $b|_B$ in $M_{n+1}U(B)$. Let $Z$ be the coproduct of $h_B$ indexed by these triples, with boundary $Z\to M$ given by $b|_B$ and map $Z\to U_{n+1}$ given by $x_{A,b,u}$. It has at most $\mu\cdot\mu=\mu$ summands. Every section $b$ of $M(A)$ lifts locally through $Z\to M$, using the chosen sieve $R_{A,b}$, so that map is epi after sheafification by the reverse implication of the same cited criterion. Each chosen section $x$ determines a formal-family component map by Step 2; its boundary therefore is a compatible cone of formal-family maps.

source.place: Lemma 5.4, pp. 13-14, applied to the matching map, with the explicit bound used in Proposition 6.6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-split-attachment-operators] to the split truncated formal family $V$ and the new family $Z$ with the boundary cone just constructed. The extension has degree $n+1$ equal to $Z\amalg\coprod_{r\leq n,\,\sigma:[n+1]\twoheadrightarrow[r]}N_r$, where $N_r$ is the family of nondegenerate summands of $V_r$, and agrees strictly with the previous family below that degree. The cited statement supplies the simplicial operators, their boundary formulas, and the normalized action of proper epis with invertible components. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-site-split-attachment-split], which gives splitness of the extension. Define its map to $U_{n+1}$ on $Z$ by the sections chosen above, and on the summand $(\sigma,i)$ by $U(\sigma)f_r$ on $N_{r,i}$. On new summands its faces agree with $f$ by the chosen boundary equation. On an old summand, a face $\alpha:[q]\to[n+1]$ gives $U(\alpha)U(\sigma)f_r=U(\sigma\alpha)f_r$, which equals $f_qV(\sigma\alpha)$ by old naturality. Proper epis agree because both apply the same concatenated epi label, with the inverse normalization cancelling the old degeneracy isomorphism. Every ordinal map factors into an epi and a face inclusion, so this proves naturality for every operator, including nonidentity top endomorphisms. The augmentation agrees because all boundary cones and $f$ are over $h_T$. There are finitely many epi labels in this degree, so the degree still has at most $\mu$ summands. Its matching map contains $Z\to M$ as a summand and is locally surjective, hence epi after sheafification by [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts].

source.place: Tag 0DAV (lemma-hypercovering-object), split attachment construction; Tag 0DAU (lemma-split). Used only through the cited general formal-family attachment statements; no finite-limit hypothesis on the site is used.

proof.text: Iterate the induction. Because every extension restricts strictly to the preceding truncated family, define $V_q$ and each operator between degrees $p,q$ using any stage at least $\max(p,q)$; strict restriction makes this independent of the stage. The identity, composition, augmentation and naturality equations hold at that finite stage, hence for the assembled augmented simplicial presheaf and the map $V\to U$. Each matching condition uses only a finite stage and is covering by construction. Thus $V\to h_T$ is a hypercover refining $U$ over the same target. Its total summand set is a countable union of sets of size at most $\mu$, so its size is at most $\mu<\kappa$.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Proposition 6.6 proof (p. 19); explicit cardinal and recursion details supplied here.

proof.text: Finally bounded hypercovers are essentially small. Relabel the summands in each degree by an ordinal below $\kappa$. The target, the object labels of all summands, and the component arrows of each simplicial operator are drawn from fixed small sets: $\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal C$, $\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal C$, and index sets of cardinality at most $\mu$. By Step 2 these data encode all presheaf operators and augmentations. There are only countably many ordinal maps between finite ordinals; all these codes therefore form a set in the working universe. The simplicial identities and matching-cover condition select a subset. Every hypercover with fewer than $\kappa$ total summands is isomorphic over its target to one of these codes. Choose a representative from each isomorphism class, obtaining a small set $\mathcal H_0$. Given $U$, Step 7 supplies bounded $V\to U$; composing with an isomorphism from its chosen representative produces a refinement from a member of $\mathcal H_0$ over the same $T$. This is the stated density.

lean.statement: theorem exists_small_dense_representable_hypercovers {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u w}, Cardinal.aleph0 < κ ∧ κ.IsRegular ∧ Cardinal.lift.{max u w} (Cardinal.mk (Σ X Y : C, (X ⟶ Y))) < κ ∧ (∀ (T : C) (U : AugmentedOver.{u, w} C T), IsHypercover J (augmentedOverToAugmented U) → ∃ V : AugmentedOver.{u, w} C T, IsHypercover J (augmentedOverToAugmented V) ∧ HasSummandBound V κ ∧ Nonempty (V ⟶ U)) ∧ ∃ (I : C → Type (max u w)) (H : ∀ T : C, I T → AugmentedOver.{u, w} C T), (∀ (T : C) (i : I T), IsHypercover J (augmentedOverToAugmented (H T i)) ∧ HasSummandBound (H T i) κ) ∧ (∀ (T : C) (U : AugmentedOver.{u, w} C T), IsHypercover J (augmentedOverToAugmented U) → HasSummandBound U κ → ∃! i : I T, Nonempty (H T i ≅ U)) ∧ (∀ (T : C) (U : AugmentedOver.{u, w} C T), IsHypercover J (augmentedOverToAugmented U) → ∃ i : I T, Nonempty (H T i ⟶ U))
